steps.name: Burly Tschäggättä
steps.text: Hrrh! Hah!

steps.name: Out-of-Breath Tschäggättä
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Exhausted Tschäggättä
steps.text: Hah....! Hraggh!

steps.name: Pumped-Up Tschäggättä
steps.text: Take this!

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: Haah—! Charge!
Have none of you had anything to eat today?
Again.

steps.name: Exhausted Tschäggättä
steps.text: Ma'am... W-We can't anymore. We're spent...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Get up.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: What did I teach you?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Stand up, and grip your weapons tight!

steps.name: Pumped-Up Tschäggättä
steps.text: Yes, ma'am!

steps.name: Out-of-Breath Tschäggättä
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*... Hargh!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Too slow, and not enough force. Your Arts are too rushed, and your tactics too inflexible.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: There's some synergy among you. That's about it.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Overall, you're still too weak.

steps.name: Burly Tschäggättä
steps.text: Of course we're no match for you...

steps.name: Exhausted Tschäggättä
steps.text: *huff*... *pant*...

steps.name: Exhausted Tschäggättä
steps.text: A compliment from you makes this training more than worth it.

steps.name: Pumped-Up Tschäggättä
steps.text: That's not enough! One day, I'll shatter a boulder with a single bare hand just like you, ma'am!

steps.name: Out-of-Breath Tschäggättä
steps.text: Just you alone...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Looks like you've had enough rest.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Do it again.

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: Huh—?!

steps.name: Frantic Tschäggättä
steps.text: Ma'am! This is bad!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Don't panic.

steps.name: Frantic Tschäggättä
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Frantic Tschäggättä
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Frantic Tschäggättä
steps.text: There's trouble!

steps.name: Frantic Tschäggättä
steps.text: Things are looking bad at the foot of the mountain... We can't handle it on our own!

steps.name: Frantic Tschäggättä
steps.text: It's real serious, ma'am! You should head right over!

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Whoa! It's starting to move!

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Hahahahaha! Mom, hurry!

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: —Wah!

steps.name: Irritated Mother
steps.text: That's why I told you not to run around on the train! Are you hurt?!

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Look, Mom! A foreigner with a funny hat!

steps.name: Irritated Mother
steps.text: Don't say things like that! And don't point at people! The Saintess has no patience for rude children! Now apologize!

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Irritated Mother
steps.text: I am truly sorry, Sir. You'll have to forgive my boy.

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: No bother.

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: Please excuse me. My seat is just up ahead.

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (The train is, evidently, above capacity.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Roughly half locals and half sightseers. Hm, peculiar for a sightseeing train.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (The sacks in the corner at the back seem strange, too... There's movement inside. Contraband livestock, perhaps?)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Hm, no other abnormalities, and no strange characters worth keeping an eye on...)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Intelligence mentions nothing other than a train ride to Lake Silberneherze. Indeed, there are no apparent clues.)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (I should find the opportunity to inspect the cabins...)
*Thump*.
*Thump* *thump*.
For the past few moments, he has been feeling a kind of strange tremor in his seatback.
Is there perhaps some strange beast that kicks seatbacks on Kjerag's trains?
*thump* *thump* *thump*.
As though dissatisfied with his indifference, the kicking intensifies.
After a moment, the child sitting behind him pokes his head out.

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Mister Funny Hat, Mister Funny Hat.

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Are you some kind of train freak? I saw you two days ago, too!

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: You saw me...?

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Yep!

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Mister, did you fall in love with trains because you had never seen tracks or trains?

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: Mister, why did you clear your throat? It's okay. I'm not gonna make fun of you.

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: This train is really amazing. I love it, too! Mom told me that it's all thanks to the amazing Saintess and Sir Enciodes and how Kjeragandr has blessed us all!

steps.name: Mischievous Child
steps.text: How about... I lend you my model train? We can play trains! We'll drive a train together!

steps.name: Irritated Mother
steps.text: Put your toys away! Go back to your seat and stop bothering strangers!

steps.name: Irritated Mother
steps.text: I'm truly, terribly sorry that he bothered you again.

steps.name: Irritated Mother
steps.text: Rest assured, I'll teach him some manners!

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: No, it's fine...

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (This hat...)

steps.name: Foreigner With a Funny Hat
steps.text: (Does it really look so strange?)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: There are quite a few passengers today. It seems this new Kjeragandr statue is very popular!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Every time I get on the trains here, it reminds me of the arenas of the Kazimierz Major—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Yow! Something bit my toe!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Is this... a fowlbeast?

steps.name: Runaway Fowlbeast
steps.text: (Biting hard)

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: O-Ow-Oww, please have mercy, fowlbeast!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You're going to just let it go?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You sure that's alright? I'm pretty sure pets aren't allowed on the train.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Indeed, that's the rule, but not everything is inspected so closely. They do cut their fellow countrymen some slack every now and then.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Relax. This kind of fowlbeast is usually kept in sacks. It should be no problem.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Let us speak of other things. Come, young lady, my cabin is just ahead.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Phew... Hah!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Finally, a seat! It was so crowded back there!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I didn't expect tickets for this train to be so hard to come by. Thanks for the help, dedushka!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It was the least I could do, young lady.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: No need for the fancy title. Just call me Rosalind.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: As the young lady wishes...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: 'Rosalind.' It's a name that suits you well. A riveting sound to it.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: It is pretty great, isn't it? My mamochka picked it.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: What do I call you?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: My name is Harold. Of course, you can also keep calling me 'dedushka,' if please you.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You're very lucky. Had you missed this train, you likely would not make it to Lake Silberneherze in time.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: For real?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hehe, good thing I made it, then.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You're heading to Lake Silberneherze too, aren't you? What are you doing there?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I believe I've already answered this question?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Kjerag's landscapes are truly magnificent. Of course I must feast my eyes upon the sights she has to offer.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You can't fool me. There's not a single guy in your whole gang who looks like a tourist.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: We don't look the part to you?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Nope.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Uh, you look more like you came looking for trouble.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Ah, haha. Us? Perish the thought!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm so enamored of Kjerag's scenery and culture. I'm even contemplating spending my retirement here!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Yes, right, so long as there are no major issues, we shall remain nothing but tourists, naturally...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: And what if—

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: —How about you, Rosalind?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You speak the Kjerag tongue fairly well for a tourist. Is this your first time here?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Somebody's changing the subject hard and fast!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Whatever. I didn't get to this part, did I?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: You could call me half Kjerag, even if I don't really feel like one at all. I grew up in Ursus with my mamochka.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Oh, so your mother is Ursine?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Yep, but she told me I was born in Kjerag, and my papa is from here...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I don't remember much about anything that happened when I was a kid. I guess you could call this a vacation.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Hmm, I see.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: By the way, I've been meaning to ask since we met...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: What is that box you are holding, Rosalind?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Oh, this...?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Forgive me. If that intrudes upon your privacy in any way, you need not answer.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: It's okay. It's not really a secret or anything. I'm just figuring out how to explain it...

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: It's something that... my mamochka left to me.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: My...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Please accept my condolences.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I am sorry to raise such a painful topic, Rosalind.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Truly sorry.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Hmph, what's so painful about this?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: I'm here to fulfill Mamochka's wishes.

steps.name: Burdenbeast Herder
steps.text: Madam Degenbrecher, I...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Everything is okay now.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I've taken care of everything that needs taking care of.

steps.name: Burdenbeast Herder
steps.text: Thank you so much, Madam.

steps.name: Burdenbeast Herder
steps.text: If it wasn't for you, who knows what would have happened to me? Thank Kjeragandr I'm still alive.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: This is all that I can do.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Sorry. It's not... a pretty sight.

steps.name: Burdenbeast Herder
steps.text: *sigh*. There wasn't any other way...

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: Ma'am, you have blood all over you. Maybe you should clean up first?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Later.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Time is of the essence. Even though I may have solved the problem for now, I can't guarantee this will be the end of it.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: The most important thing is to find the one we're looking for.

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: But, ma'am, we got news that they're already leaving the station.

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: Asking the railway to stop the train would only cause a panic.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Stop the train?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: There's no need for that.

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: What else can we do?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Look down.

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: Wait...

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: The train is about to pass right under us!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: Wait, m-ma'am?!
Her figure as she descends upon the train seems both lighter than snow and heavier than stone.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Right then.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Where might they be?
